.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Hot, humid conditions persist into next week, 
along with daily chances for shower and thunderstorms.

A very repetitive weather pattern has set up for the next 
several days, characterized by warm and humid air from offshore 
high pressure and continued impulses of upper level energy. This
will yield showers and storms each day through at least early 
next week, and likely even beyond. 

Friday looks somewhat similar to what we are seeing today, 
albeit with slightly more shear/forcing. A slightly more potent 
piece of energy looks to move across the area during peak 
heating. This should yield deep-layer shear values closer to 30 
knots perhaps. There will be a similar thermodynamic environment
in place, with high amounts of CAPE, but DCAPE values similar 
or even a bit less than today. One thing to watch for though is 
that, thanks to the shortwave, mid-level lapse rates will be in 
the 6-7 C/km range tomorrow afternoon, which could lead to a 
higher coverage of stronger updrafts. This would then allow more
storms to potentially tap into that peak downdraft potential 
and yield a few more severe storms than we see this afternoon. 
Would also expect to see some large hail as well, given the 
higher lapse rates aloft. A Marginal Risk is maintained from the
Storm Prediction Center. 

Beyond Friday, this pattern likely continues through at least
the early and middle portions of next week. South to 
southwesterly flow is maintained over the Mid-Atlantic. Hot and 
humid conditions each afternoon, with highs reaching the upper 
80s to low 90s, and heat indices in the low 100s each of the 
Blue Ridge. Scattered showers and thunderstorms each afternoon.
Deep layer shear is forecast to increase through the weekend as
the subtropical jet stream strengthens. On Saturday, a more 
potent shortwave trough is forecast to move overhead that could 
aid in stronger, more organized severe convection. Damaging wind
gusts will be the main threat.

A quasi-zonal flow aloft will develop Sunday into into next week. 
Sunday could bring a short reprieve as dry conditions prevail.
However, seasonably hot and humid conditions continue, and
should quickly bring showers and storms back into the forecast 
Monday through most of next week. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Patchy dense fog will be possible over the next several
mornings.

With daily showers and thunderstorms, and warm/humid overnights,
patchy dense fog can be expected each morning. The location 
will be difficult to pinpoint, with areas that receive rain the 
day prior the likely candidates. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...A cold front could arrive late in the week, 
potentially bringing a pattern change into next weekend. 

While this is very far out in the forecast period, there is some
signal that a more potent frontal system could push through the
region late in the week. The details are murky at this stage of
the forecast, with timing very uncertain, as well as potential
impacts. Guidance is generally between Thursday/Friday right
now, with improvement in the weather pattern possible 
thereafter. Any decent frontal passage in the summer time should
be watched closely for potential severe weather, so we will 
keep monitoring this in the coming days to see if that potential
is there, and try to narrow down the timeframe a bit more.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...

VFR conditions prevail for most of the time through early next 
week. South to southwest winds prevail for the foreseeable 
future as the Bermuda high persists across the western Atlantic.
Daily chances for showers and thunderstorms each afternoon and 
evening through the middle of next week, which could result in 
periods of restrictions at affected terminals.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories could be needed for parts of the waters at 
times through Saturday, mainly in the late afternoon to evening.
Most days will be marginal, and likely handled by MWSs, but just
know it could get a bit breezy over the open waters each
afternoon. Otherwise, winds remain around 10 knots. Daily 
showers and thunderstorms expected each afternoon into next 
early week. Special Marine Warnings would accompany any of the 
stronger thunderstorms capable of producing frequent lightning 
and wind gusts over 35 knots.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Anomalies climb late this week in response to return southerly flow. 
Periods of coastal flooding are possible at times of high tide at 
sensitive locations.
